title: Beylik of Tunis
capsule: The Husainid Beylik of Tunis was founded in 1705 when Husain ibn Ali, an Ottoman-appointed officer, established a hereditary dynasty that governed Tunisia as a semi-autonomous Ottoman province. At its height the beylik maintained its own military, concluded commercial treaties with European powers, and controlled a prosperous corsair economy centered on Tunis and the Saharan trade routes; Hammuda Pasha (r. 1782–1814) was its most capable ruler. France invaded in April–May 1881 under the pretext of border raids, imposing the Treaty of Bardo (12 May 1881) which established a French protectorate and ended effective Husainid sovereignty; the 1885 end-date in the batch reflects the consolidation of French administrative control.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The beylik's territory within the historical Ifriqiya/Tunisia region is well documented; southern desert boundaries with adjacent tribal zones are approximate.
